newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ CPI shows RB inflation band responsible-Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ CPI shows RB inflation band responsible-Peters.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters said on Tuesday that March quarter consumer price data showed responsible inflation targets could be achieved under the Reserve Bank's widened 0-3 percent band.

Peters said the CPI data released earlier on Tuesday, from which the Reserve Bank calculated underlying inflation at 0.22 percent in the March quarter and 1.97 percent in the March year, also showed the government's forecasting was about on track.

"We're very happy with today's result, it says that our forecasting is about on track," Peters told journalists after addressing the Association of Investment Advisers and Financial Planners on the proposed compulsory pensions savings scheme. "What have we demonstrated? That you can obtain responsible targets with a wider band. We've proven that the fear of some poeple is not correct. We're very, very happy with today's result."

The Reserve Bank's target band for underlying inflation was widened to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent in December last year when Peters' NZ First party formed a coalition government with the National Party.
The proposed pensions scheme, advocated by New Zealand First, will go to a public referendum in September.
